key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN surrogate can accurately predict friction stir welding temperatures, forces, and defect formation in HDPE, enabling fast identification of robust process windows.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical welding guidance showing that bottom preheating and higher rotation/lower travel speed improve weld quality while reducing force fluctuations and wormhole defects.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force histories
Process-map generation across rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R2 values of 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL model matched experiments for void formation, thermal response, and vertical force behavior.
watch_item: The trained models are validated on the tested parameter space, so extrapolation to other polymers, tool geometries, or wider process ranges may be unreliable without retraining.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
